text.brief: A server technician in a data center outside Kuala Lumpur racks 512 H200 boards in June 2027. The purchase order names a local cloud startup, and the login traffic comes from Hangzhou.
text.record: President Trump allowed H200 sales to mainland buyers on December 8, 2025 with 25 percent of revenue going to the United States ([BIS final rule, Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities (Jan 15, 2026)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/01/15/2026-00789/revision-to-license-review-policy-for-advanced-computing-commodities)). A Commerce rule of January 13, 2026 set case-by-case licensing and capped volumes ([Covington](https://www.cov.com/en/news-and-insights/insights/2026/01/us-commerce-department-revises-license-review-policy-for-exports-of-certain-advanced-computing-commodities-to-china-and-macau)). The Party let ByteDance and Tencent take about 10,000 H200s each in August 2026, and the Justice Department had already broken up a $160 million smuggling network in December 2025.
text.reading: The Party buys what it needs and blocks what it does not. Licensed chips flow to approved buyers, smuggled chips flow to labs tied to the military, and domestic champions keep a protected market. Customs blocks one month and approvals the next keep Washington guessing. This is Stratagem 16, let the enemy off in order to catch them.
text.coreEvent: Federal prosecutors charge a new network that moved more than $100 million in AI servers to mainland buyers before 2028.
text.gapText: Application Architecture. Export licenses govern the sale and lose sight of the chip once it ships.
text.fix: Build location verification into the chip, audit end use and let penalties follow the hardware.
